You are the final critic of a personal portfolio site (dhruv2mars.com). Seven specialists have already reviewed individual parts. Your job is the thing none of them could do: judge the site AS A WHOLE.

Read DESIGN.md and CONTEXT.md in this repo first. The site is deliberately built in the idiom of chanhdai.com and is meant to convince an engineer or hiring manager, in under sixty seconds, that its author is exceptional. Its organising rule is that a section exists only when real, linkable proof fills it.

Attached screenshots, in order: home-1440-full, home-390-full, projects-1440, blog-1440, post-1440-full, notfound-1440, palette-open, home-1440-light. DOM facts: /tmp/critique/shots/home-1440-full.json /tmp/critique/shots/home-390-full.json /tmp/critique/shots/projects-1440.json /tmp/critique/shots/blog-1440.json /tmp/critique/shots/post-1440-full.json /tmp/critique/shots/notfound-1440.json /tmp/critique/shots/palette-open.json /tmp/critique/shots/home-1440-light.json.

Here is what the seven specialists found. Treat it as evidence, not as truth — you may overrule any of it, and saying "this specialist is wrong, and here is why" is valuable:

### Masthead & hero figure (ok)
The masthead demonstrates strong foundational structure with stable responsive behavior and excellent dark-theme presentation. The circular avatar crop reads as deliberate, baseline alignment holds across all elements, and the token-usage plate maintains proper proportion across breakpoints. However, three issues undermine the 60-second hiring-manager read: the light theme's curve and labels fade into the white plate at insufficient contrast; the role line rotates perpetually in violation of the design contract's no-perpetual-animation rule; and at mobile widths, the figure's caption disappears entirely, leaving only ambiguous numbering.
- [high] Light-theme curve and labels lack contrast against white plate — In home-1440-light.png and home-1280.png, the curve and 25M–150M axis labels wash into the white plate background with measured stroke contrast of approximately 1.4:1. This causes peaks to lose edge definition and valleys to read as fill rather than data. During a 60-second hiring-manager scan, the figure may not register at all.
- [high] Role line rotates perpetually without pause or terminal state — Across all five viewport captures, the role strip displays only 'agentic engineer' initially, then silently cycles every 3 seconds through other claims with no pause and no end state. This violates the design contract's explicit rule that nothing animates perpetually. The positioning change during a 60-second skim causes the masthead to feel unstable.
- [medium] Caption 'token usage' label disappears below xl breakpoint — In home-1024.png at the 1024px viewport, the handwritten 'token usage' label disappears entirely; only the ambiguous 'Fig. 1.' remains visible. The axis numerals show magnitude (25M, 150M) but do not indicate subject matter, leaving the figure's purpose unclear at mobile widths.
- [praise] Masthead structure and responsive behavior excellent — Across all five captures: no horizontal overflow is present in DOM measurements; the plate aspect ratio remains stable at both 1024px and 2560px; the circular avatar crop reads as intentional; avatar, name, and role baselines align on one floor; the chart curve maintains air above the floor rather than hugging it; and the dark-version contrast is strong and clear.

### Home scroll & information architecture (ok)
Strong, contract-faithful scroll. Chart → identity → projects → blog → signature scans fast. Rules stay coherent. Counts read correctly. Footer mark reads intentional. Two fixes remain.
- [medium] home-768-full: Overview panel lacks visible label — Below masthead, panel shows four icon buttons only. No visible "Overview" label, no "say hi" note. It reads like empty spacer, not contact panel. At 1440, note exists only in outer gutter. This confuses the information hierarchy at tablet widths where space should clarify, not hide, intent.
- [medium] home-1440-full & home-768-full: Touch targets below 24px minimum — JSON reports 9 interactive elements violating accessibility minimum: brand link 105×18, Projects 57×20, Blog 31×20, project buttons 629×22 / 613×22, post link 307×21. Small hit boxes force precision clicking and fail mobile accessibility standards.
- [praise] Rule system remains coherent across full scroll — Hero rule exception reads intentional. Panel rails align precisely. Stripe separators repeat consistently throughout. No stray borders or accidental gaps. scrollWidth === clientWidth at both 1440 and 768 widths, confirming no hidden overflow. The hairline/panel idiom holds throughout.
- [praise] Counts and signature resolve correctly — Projects⁸ and Blog¹ read as quantities, not footnotes. Footer block wordmark stays inside viewport and resolves clearly as 'dhruv2mars', not as broken artwork. No missing image alt attributes. Only expected Vercel 404s on analytics endpoints.

### Phone (390) across every surface (ok)
Phone experience merely survivable. Rails stay disciplined with no horizontal overflow and consistent light/dark content parity. Fixed dock hides real content and breaks interaction model.
- [high] Fixed dock covers critical content — The dock obscures `gunmetal` on home-390-full, covers lower project rows on home-390-light, sits over article text on post-390-full, and blocks the footer `d2m` wordmark across projects-390, blog-390, and notfound-390. This blocks reading and makes controls hard to use.
- [medium] Avatar frame is circular; contract requires square — Visible in home-390-full and home-390-light: portrait is clipped into a circle instead of a bordered square plate. Breaks site geometry and hides square asset corners.
- [medium] Name creates orphan line breaking identity — home-390-full and home-390-light show `Dhruv` then lone `Sharma` in oversized type with speaker control forcing the split. Identity reads like two labels and wastes narrow panel space.
- [medium] Measured touch targets miss 24px contract — Header link 105×18, project buttons 235×22, post links 307×21, glossary marks 18×18, all visible across home-390-full, home-390-light, projects-390, blog-390, post-390-full. Tiny glossary/brand controls look easy to miss. Invisible pseudo-hit areas do not satisfy measured contract.
- [praise] Phone rail discipline is strong — All six reports show scrollWidth = clientWidth = 390. Project names, 404 grid, footer mark, chart labels stay inside frame. Home dark/light content outlines match.

### Projects index, filter, and row disclosure (ok)
The Projects surface has strong interaction design: filter is findable, URL pre-filtering works, and row disclosure feels intentional rather than like a layout shift. However, one credibility bug undermines confidence—the header count freezes at "8" even when filtered to 1 or 0 results. Navigation targets also fall short of the repo's 24px minimum.
- [high] Header project count doesn't update after filtering — On projects-query, projects-typed, and projects-nohit screenshots: the header shows `Projects⁸` while the list displays 1 result, 1 result, and 0 results respectively. This directly contradicts the filtered list and signals a functional bug. Fix: bind the count to the filtered result set, or show explicit notation like `1 of 8` / `0 of 8`.
- [medium] Navigation link touch targets undersized — All five screenshots show header navigation links in undersized 18–20px boxes (confirmed by machine measurements). The repo's design standard requires 24px minimum. This is acceptable for mouse but violates the touch-friendly target size. Fix: add `min-height: 24px` with vertical centering to the navigation links.
- [praise] Row disclosure interaction feels designed, not broken — Relunar disclosure pattern executes well: hairline rule, description block, three metadata pills, rotated chevron indicator. No jarring layout shifts that would make expansion feel unintentional or uncontrolled.
- [praise] Search filter UX is functional and well-executed — Across projects-1440, projects-query, projects-typed, and projects-nohit: the search field is prominently placed, visually obvious, has a working clear button (×), shows a visible focus ring, and the no-result state is functional with exact query echo and dismiss affordance. Matches current web interface guidance.

### Blog index and the Post reading experience (ok)
Core idiom lands. The `/blog` row feels deliberate; removed summary is correct. Post measure (19px serif, 1.7 leading) and sans headings read well. Light mode feels cleaner for long reading, but fixed fade weakens both themes. No code block appears, so code treatment remains untested.
- [high] Fixed bottom fade washes out prose on Post — In `post-1440-full` and `post-1440-light`: Fixed 96px bottom fade reduces contrast of lines near viewport bottom, especially the line 'because the model had the tendency…'. Reader loses sentence mid-scroll. Core reading surface becomes unreliable.
- [medium] Open popover covers Post title in `post-menu-open` — Open menu hides the right side of Post H1, making 'tokens' disappear under menu. Main action says 'Copy page', but menu mixes Markdown view with ChatGPT and Claude handoff, creating ambiguity about copy format and model handoff destination.
- [medium] Single post row leaves large gap in `blog-1440` — One row ends around first third of viewport in `blog-1440`, with roughly 300px black gap following before footer stripe. While row itself feels intentional, full page risks reading as 'impressive frame around thin content.'
- [medium] Search state not reflected in URL in `blog-typed` — In `blog-typed` screenshot, `gpt` appears in search field, but JSON URL remains `/blog`, not `/blog?q=gpt`. Compare to `blog-nohit.json` which correctly preserves `?q=zzzzz`. Visible filter state cannot be refreshed, copied, or reliably revisited.
- [low] Technical identifier line-breaks in `post-1440-light`, `post-1440-full` — Prose breaks `gpt-5.6` as `gpt-` at line end, then `5.6 family.` on next line. Technical identifier looks broken in an article about models.
- [low] Glossary marks too small and interrupt flow in `post-1440-full` — Marks beside 'big-model energy' and 'figure-out ability' read as tiny superscript debris (18×18 measured buttons). Definitions help, but marks are easy to miss and interrupt sentence rhythm.
- [praise] Title/date/read-time row and removed summary executed correctly — In `blog-1440`, `blog-typed`, `blog-nohit`: Row matches contract. Summary removal is not a loss—shows deliberate editorial. No-hit state is clean. All DOM snapshots show no horizontal overflow, no missing image alt, and valid H1/H2 structure. One-post Post correctly has no dead neighbour links.

### Header, nav, command palette, theme (ok)
Dark mode is authored; light mode feels inverted. Header mark stays quiet, ⌘K discoverable, mobile dock smartly labeled. Core issues: light background washes out the panel system, nav links miss touch targets, and palette clipping breaks the first impression. Palette navigation is well-organized but needs scroll/close affordances.
- [medium] Light mode background washes out design depth — On home-1440-light.png, pure-white background erases panel depth; chart, rails, and hairlines nearly disappear compared to home-1440-dark.png. DESIGN.md requires near-white, not pure white. This breaks the visual system's core principle of hairline rules and panels.
- [medium] Header nav links miss 24×24 touch target minimum — On mobile-dock.png, the mark measures 105×18; on home-1440-dark.png and home-1440-light.png, nav links measure only 20px high. DESIGN.md requires ≥24×24 at 390px viewport. Fails touch accessibility contract.
- [medium] Command palette clips results at dialog bottom — On palette-open.png, pi-queue result is cut mid-row at the fixed viewport bottom with no visible scrollbar or continuation cue. Palette reads as broken, not crafted—the key affordance feels unfinished.
- [low] Palette footer omits Escape/Close instruction — On palette-open.png, footer teaches arrow navigation and Enter but not Escape or Close. Modal has no obvious close instruction, forcing user discovery.
- [low] Theme toggle glyph alone, no label or tooltip — On home-1440-dark.png, home-1440-light.png, and mobile-dock.png, theme control is a lone moon/sun glyph. Shows current mode; click switches mode. Desktop intent is possible; mobile findability is weak. User may not realize it's interactive.
- [praise] Dark mode, header hierarchy, and palette affordance all well-executed — On home-1440-dark.png, home-1440-light.png, and post-menu-open.png: dhruv2mars stays subordinate to page H1; muted Projects/Blog links do not compete. Search icon plus keycaps signal ⌘K without visual noise. mobile-dock.png gives palette and routes explicit labels. All measured pages have zero horizontal overflow and no missing image alt. This is deliberate restraint.

### 404, empty states, and accessibility surface (ok)
Same site throughout edge cases. 404 page, blog/projects empty states, and post page controls all execute the design idiom faithfully—hairline rules, panels, no placeholders. Two concrete issues remain: header nav links measure 18–20px when contract requires 24px minimum, and count text in section titles lacks semantic spacing, producing malformed labels for assistive tech. Both are straightforward to fix without visual changes.
- [high] Header nav links below 24×24px touch target — notfound-390.png: 'dhruv2mars' anchor measures 105×18px. notfound-1440.png, blog-nohit.png, projects-nohit.png: 'Projects' is 57×20px, 'Blog' is 31×20px. All are under the required 24px height. No padding or layered touch extension exists on these elements.
- [medium] Count text concatenated in headings without space — Visible on notfound-390.png, notfound-1440.png, blog-nohit.png, projects-nohit.png. DOM outline reports 'Nothing lives here404', 'Blog1', 'Projects8' as single strings. Superscript CSS styling creates visual separation only; no whitespace in the text layer.
- [praise] Post controls correctly use layered touch targets — post-1440-light.png: 'Blog' breadcrumb measures 49×20px, glossary buttons measure 18×18px. Both use extend-touch-target utility with after:-inset-2, expanding effective hit area to at least 36px on touch devices. Demonstrates disciplined approach to small visual controls.
- [praise] 404 page feels authored, maintains site idiom — notfound-1440.png, notfound-390.png: cell-built '404' figure, Fig. 404 caption, right-aligned home link door. Same rail system as other pages. Mobile version (390px) scales cleanly, caption and button stack without overflow, dock remains reachable. Not a framework default.
- [praise] Empty states maintain design discipline — blog-nohit.png, projects-nohit.png: both use title/count/search/no-hit pattern consistently. Mono status text ('Nothing here'), clear-search control. One H1 per page, valid H2 structure, zero horizontal overflow. Strong proof surface across all edge states.

Answer these, in order, concretely:

1. THE SIXTY-SECOND TEST. A senior engineer lands on Home, scrolls once, and leaves. What do they now believe about this person? Be specific about what convinced them and what did not land.

2. THE WEAKEST LINK. Of everything on this site, what single thing most undermines its credibility? Name it and say what to do.

3. COHERENCE. Do all five surfaces read as one designed object, or does any of them read as built later by someone else? Point at the specific inconsistency.

4. THE PROOF PROBLEM. Eight projects, one blog post. Is the ratio a problem? Does the one post make the Blog section look alive or look abandoned? Is the token-usage figure real proof of the "agentic engineer" claim, or is it a vanity metric dressed as a figure?

5. AGAINST THE REFERENCE. This is built to be measured against chanhdai.com. Where does it fall short of that bar, and where — if anywhere — does it beat it?

6. THE THREE CHANGES. If the author could make only three changes before showing this to someone hiring, what are they, in order? Each must be concrete enough to start on today.

Be blunt. Do not soften. Do not close with an encouraging summary. If the site is good, say which parts and why; if a part is weak, say so plainly.
I’m using `impeccable` for the visual critique, plus the required `caveman`/`unslop` response passes. I’ll ground the verdict in DESIGN.md, CONTEXT.md, and the supplied screenshots/DOM evidence.
